title: Terraform JSON: sensitivity flags, unknown or null values and write-only version counters with no value present
summary: Synthetic Terraform JSON excerpts that carry the sensitivity metadata of a password but not its value: a plan whose write-only password argument is absent and whose password_wo_version counter is the integer 1, a plan whose password is unknown until apply (after_unknown and after_sensitive are true, no value), and a state in which the password attribute is null while sensitive_values marks it true.
rationale: These are the contrast to the sensitive attribute written as a plain string. The key is named password, the flag says sensitive and the name ends in _wo or _wo_version, yet the document holds no secret bytes: a boolean true, a null, an absent key and a version counter. The failure mode is reacting to the credential-shaped key or flag instead of the value, and treating a write-only argument as stored. Terraform documents that a write-only value is discarded and only its version argument is stored, that the sensitivity structures hold only true, and that unknown and null values are absent or null.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged. No secret value is present in any of the three documents: HashiCorp documents that Terraform discards a write-only argument value without storing it in the plan or state file and stores only the version argument, that the after_sensitive and sensitive_values structures replace sensitive leaves with true, that after_unknown replaces unknown leaves with true, and that unknown and null values are treated as absent or null. The documents are synthetic compositions of these documented shapes (origin: evidence-derived). Twin of the case with the literal present: only the value slot differs. Not established: how a given provider populates a null or omitted attribute for a write-only field; the fixtures state only the documented shapes.

sources.supports: During a Terraform operation, the provider uses the password_wo value to create the database instance, and then Terraform discards that value without storing it in the plan or state file.

Providers implement version arguments to let practitioners track write-only argument values and control when a provider uses those write-only arguments. [...] Terraform stores version arguments in state, and can track if a version argument changes.
sources.locator: section: Update write-only arguments with versions

sources.supports: "after_unknown" is an object value with similar structure to "after", but with all unknown leaf values replaced with "true", and all known leaf values omitted.
Unknown values and null values are both treated as absent or null.

"before_sensitive" and "after_sensitive" are object values with similar structure to "before" and "after", but with all sensitive leaf values replaced with true, and all non-sensitive leaf values omitted.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
